name: Value Creation, Distribution & Management
question: Is real economic value being created (customers pay more than it costs to serve them), is it distributed sanely (customers/employees/shareholders), and does management allocate capital like owners?

signals.description: Unit economics evidence: gross margin, cash conversion; summary.schema extraction of revenue, GM, OCF, FCF, SBC, share count — each figure cited to its filing

recipe.query_template: {company} annual report OR quarterly filing revenue gross margin cash flow

signals.description: Earnings quality: cash flow tracking net income; extraction of OCF vs NI divergence across periods

recipe.query_template: {company} operating cash flow versus net income

signals.description: Dilution discipline: share count and SBC trajectory; extraction across filings

recipe.query_template: {company} share count OR stock-based compensation trajectory

signals.description: Capital allocation: buybacks vs price history, M&A discipline, capex returns; filings + news, Alpaca price context (US)

recipe.query_template: {company} buybacks versus price history, M&A discipline, capex returns

signals.description: Insider behavior: buying vs selling patterns in coverage
Customer value evidence: retention, willingness to pay, NPS coverage — independent sources only (reviews, case studies not hosted by company)

recipe.query_template: {company} customer retention OR willingness to pay OR NPS

signals.description: Management candor: do they name mistakes, or reframe every miss? LLM tone analysis over earnings-call coverage across quarters

recipe.query_template: {company} earnings-call coverage across quarters: does management name mistakes or reframe every miss

grade_anchors.A: Cash flows confirm the income statement; dilution modest; capital returns disciplined; customers demonstrably better off; management admits and corrects errors.
grade_anchors.C: Value creation real but partially consumed by SBC/dilution; capital allocation mixed; candor selective.
grade_anchors.F: Income statement and cash flow tell different stories; value flows mainly to insiders (dilution, related-party payments, buybacks timed around insider sales); customers churn when subsidies stop.

false_signals.description: Widening gap between adjusted and GAAP earnings; "community-adjusted EBITDA" pathology. Extraction of both figures per period; trend the gap.
Net income persistently exceeding operating cash flow. Filings extraction (red-flag tier of forensic accounting; deeper accrual decomposition is v2, see §9).

recipe.query_template: {company} net income exceeding operating cash flow

false_signals.description: Accounting-policy changes coinciding with growth inflections. Filings coverage + news search for restatement/policy language.

recipe.query_template: {company} revenue recognition change OR restatement OR accounting policy change

false_signals.description: Auditor resignation/change, qualified opinions, material weaknesses, delayed filings. Monitor + filings; any hit is an automatic composite cap.

recipe.query_template: {company} auditor resignation OR auditor change OR qualified opinion OR material weakness OR delayed filing

false_signals.description: Transactions with insider-linked entities. Filings extraction of related-party sections.
Company buying back stock while insiders sell. Cross-reference buyback announcements vs insider-sale coverage.

evidence_policy.notes: Anchor framework: weighted highest and vetoes the composite (D or lower caps composite at B). v1 covers the red-flag tier of forensic accounting only; deeper accrual decomposition is v2. The round-trip-revenue composite-cap pattern is detected in F8 (round_trip_deals) and propagates here via composite_cap:C.
